s1.syndrome_frame: Jaw pain and tooth mobility with radiographic evidence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion
salient_findings: Tender percussion of the right mandibular second premolar and first molar
Slight mobility of the affected teeth
Buccolingual expansion with cortical thinning on cone beam CT
key_facts: Pain and slight mobility of the mandibular right second premolar and first molar
Slight mobility of the affected teeth
Bony-hard consistency of the buccal and lingual cortices
Lesion extends to the superior border of the inferior alveolar nerve canal
Cone beam CT shows buccolingual expansion with cortical thinning

shortlist.label: Odontogenic keratocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Matches radiographic findings of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion

shortlist.label: Unicystic ameloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the clinical presentation of jaw pain and tooth mobility, and radiographic evidence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion

shortlist.label: Radicular cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the radiolucent lesion, especially given the history of a previously endodontically treated tooth

shortlist.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to odontogenic keratocyst, with potential for aggressive behavior and matching radiographic features

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Could be a consideration given the location and radiographic appearance of the lesion, although less likely than the top three entities

raw.rationale: The unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion and cortical thinning, as well as the atypical irregular shape, are consistent with the characteristics of an odontogenic keratocyst, now more commonly referred to as a keratocystic odontogenic tumor, but given the options, odontogenic keratocyst is the closest match.

rejected.label: Unicystic ameloblastoma
rejected.why: While unicystic ameloblastoma can present as a unilocular radiolucency, it often has a more complex appearance and is less likely given the description of the lesion's shape and expansion pattern.

rejected.label: Radicular cyst
rejected.why: Radicular cysts are typically associated with the apex of a non-vital tooth and have a more rounded shape, which does not match the atypical irregular shape described in the case.

rejected.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: This is essentially the same entity as odontogenic keratocyst, with the term keratocystic odontogenic tumor being the currently preferred nomenclature, but since 'odontogenic keratocyst' is provided as an option, it is selected as the champion.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: Dentigerous cysts are associated with the crown of an unerupted tooth, which does not fit the scenario described, involving teeth that are already erupted and have been treated or are in use.
